title: Cohort analysis: defining the group and the observation window

videos.script: Panela has six thousand customers who signed up over two years. How many are still ordering? {{question}} Put that way, the question has no good answer. A customer who joined last month has had one month to leave. A customer who joined two years ago has had twenty-four. Averaging them together measures when people joined, not how long they stay. {{mixed}} A cohort analysis fixes that by lining people up by when they started. Everyone who signed up in January 2024 is one cohort. February is another. {{cohort}} Then each cohort is followed month by month from its own start: month zero, month one, month two. Every row is a group of people, and every column is the same age. {{table}} Two decisions shape everything after that. Who belongs to the group. And how the months are counted. Get the second one wrong, and customers who joined at the end of a month look less loyal than customers who joined at the start, for no reason at all. {{decisions}} This lesson builds Panela's cohort table and makes both decisions explicit. {{end}}
